This page covers three things:

- What [`src/output/vcon.rs`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/output/vcon.rs) holds.
- Which sipnab type feeds each part of the container.
- The two mechanisms an editor has to respect:
  - the duplicated completeness caveat;
  - the deterministic uuid.

Read [Export one observed call as a vCon](@/docs/vcon.md) for the operator's view.
Read [the Phase 0 decision](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/docs/design/vcon.md) for why the module refuses what it
refuses. This page is about the code.

## Shape of the module

The module is one file behind the non-default `vcon` feature. The `full` feature carries it.

- It has no submodules and no state.
- Every input arrives as an argument.
- Nothing in it reads a process global except the node name.

The public surface has these parts:

- A struct per vCon section: `Vcon`, `Party`, `Dialog`,
  `Attachment`, `Analysis`.
- `BlindSpot` and `CaptureCompleteness` for the caveat.
- `ExportContext` for everything the dialog itself does not carry.
- Three functions: [`export_dialog()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/output/vcon.rs),
  [`export_dialog_at()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/output/vcon.rs) and
  [`dialog_uuid()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/output/vcon.rs).

`export_dialog_at()` is the pure form. Every test drives it.

- Its third argument is the container's `created_at`.
- So two exports compare byte for byte.
- Any difference between them came from the capture, not from the clock.
- `export_dialog()` is the same function with `Utc::now()` supplied.

Serialization is `serde`'s. Each struct maps one-to-one onto its vCon object.

- `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"` does the work of "sipnab did
  not observe this".
- The result is an absent field, never a null.

## Where each section comes from

| vCon section | Read from | Built by |
|---|---|---|
| `vcon`, `extensions` | module constants | inline in `export_dialog_at()` |
| `uuid` | the dialog's `Call-ID` and clock, the capture id, the node name | [`dialog_uuid()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/output/vcon.rs) |
| `created_at` | the caller's clock, not the dialog's | the `exported_at` argument |
| `parties[0]`, `parties[1]` | `SipDialog`'s `from_*`/`to_*` fields, the opening message, the first response | [`observed_parties()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/output/vcon.rs) |
| `parties[].tel` | the SIP user part, only when it is an [RFC 3966](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3966.html) global number | [`tel_uri()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/output/vcon.rs) |
| `parties[last]` | [`node_name()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/provenance.rs) and the crate version | [`observer_party()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/output/vcon.rs) |
| `dialog[0]` | the `Call-ID`, the observed tags, and [`final_status_code()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/sip/dialog.rs) | [`dialog_object()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/output/vcon.rs) |
| `attachments[0]` | the message ladder, through [`message_to_json_value()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/output/json.rs) | [`message_trace_attachment()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/output/vcon.rs) |
| `attachments[1]` | `CaptureFacts` and the ranked `CaptureAnalysis` | [`completeness_attachment()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/output/vcon.rs) |
| `analysis[0]` | [`diagnose_signaling()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/sip/diagnosis.rs) and the same completeness value | [`report()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/output/vcon.rs) |

Three of those rows carry a decision rather than a mapping.

**`tel` is narrow because a wrong index entry beats no index entry only in
appearance.**

- A conserver indexes parties by `tel`, `mailto` and `name` and by
  nothing else.
- So a container with none of the three answers only to its UUID.
- `tel_uri()` supplies one for `+` followed by digits and for nothing else.
- A bare digit run is an RFC 3966 LOCAL number needing a `phone-context`.
- In SIP captures it is usually an extension. `1001` is not a telephone number.

**The message trace reuses `--json`'s projection.**

- One serializer produces both.
- So a vCon and an NDJSON line describing one message cannot disagree about it.
- The cost of that reuse is the credential strip, further down.

**The report reuses the signaling diagnosis.**

- It is already the wire shape the dialog-JSON surface emits.
- A second projection of one analysis is two definitions waiting to drift apart.

`ExportContext` exists for the same reason `CaptureFacts` does:

- It makes visible, in one place, exactly which facts a completeness claim stands on.
- It lets a test state the capture it describes instead of mutating a global.

## The completeness carrier

The whole module exists for this mechanism. An edit is most likely to break it.

sipnab's ranked problem list puts incompleteness findings **inside** the list.

- They sit at `Severity::Blind`, above every call fault.
- So "no problems found" is structurally unreachable for an incomplete read.

vCon offers no position with that property.

- `analysis[]` is a list of conclusions.
- A caveat placed there is one entry among others.

### Why duplication rather than one field

The obvious repair is a custom extension carrying the caveat. The format
rules it out. An extension is one of two kinds:

- **compatible**: a consumer that does not implement it ignores it safely;
- **critical**: a consumer that does not implement it MUST NOT process it except to reject.

There is no third level meaning *read this before trusting the contents*.

Pick either and the caveat fails.

- Ignorable: the consumer that most needs it drops it.
- Critical: an ordinary vCon reader refuses the whole container.
  - So sipnab has emitted something nobody can read.

So the caveat goes into two surfaces a consumer walks past anyway:

- `capture_completeness` inside `analysis[0].body`, beside the diagnosis.
  - `body` is the JSON object itself.
  - So a reader indexes into it directly. See below.
- An attachment with purpose `sipnab-capture-completeness`.
  - Its `party` index names the sipnab observer.

### One value, embedded twice

[`completeness_of()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/output/vcon.rs) builds **one**
`CaptureCompleteness`.

- `export_dialog_at()` then hands the same value to
  `completeness_attachment()` and to `report()`.
- Nothing rebuilds it.
- Nothing formats it a second time.

That distinction is the whole rule.

- Two strings built twice drift.
- A container whose two caveats disagree reads as authoritative while contradicting
  itself.
- That is worse than one carrying no caveat at all.

The audio exporter learned this the expensive way.

- It built its embedded note and its printed summary separately.
- A clause reached one and not the other.
- A comparison test caught it.
- This module copies that shape deliberately.

**The divergence gate is
`the_two_completeness_surfaces_carry_one_value`.**

- It exports one dialog against facts carrying two distinct losses.
- It then asserts that the attachment body and the
  report's `capture_completeness` compare equal as JSON values.
- Rebuild the caveat in either place and it fails.

Two more tests hold the ends of it:

- `the_completeness_carrier_discriminates_a_lossy_run_from_a_clean_one`:
  - It exports one dialog twice.
  - One run lost seven captured messages. The other run lost none.
  - It requires the two notes to differ.
  - Without it the carrier could be decoration: identical on every run, and equal to itself.
  - Deleting the `messages_evicted` clause fails it.
- `an_absent_analysis_is_not_a_clean_bill`:
  - It separates "nobody looked" from "looked and found nothing".
  - `blind_spots` stays absent when no analysis reached the export.
  - It becomes `[]` when one ran and ranked nothing.
  - Collapsing the two lets a run that skipped the analysis read as clean.

## The spec is the gate, not our reading of it

Two decisions in this module came from reading two sources:

- [the draft](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core/);
- the reference implementation.

They did not come from what looked natural in Rust.

- Both were wrong in the first cut.
- A hand-written test agreed with the wrong answer.
- The same misreading produced both.

**`body` takes the shape its `encoding` defines.**

- [Section 2.3.2 of the core draft](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-2.3.2)
  defines `"json"` as "The value of the body parameter is a JSON value (object,
  array, number, string, or one of the literals true, false, or null)".
- The CDDL in [Appendix C](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#appendix-C)
  states that `body` is any JSON value when `encoding` is `"json"`, and a string otherwise.
- `Attachment::body` and `Analysis::body` are `serde_json::Value`.
  - Every `json` body sipnab writes is the object itself.
- Earlier releases wrote the object's text as a string.
  - That is a JSON string value, not the object the encoding describes.
- The readers still accept that shape.
  - [`answer_body()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/app/vcon_enrich.rs) keeps a `json` body from an
    enrichment service as whatever JSON value it is.
  - The `-I` reader parses a string `json` body as JSON text.
- The gate is `every_body_has_the_shape_its_encoding_defines`, in the ingest
  contract test named under the schema gate below.

**core-03 had two defects on this one field, and core-04 settled both.**

- The first was a vocabulary gap.
  - None of the five type values described a conversation known to have occurred
    whose content the container does not carry or reference.
  - That is the ordinary result for an observer that retains no media.
- The second was a prose/schema inconsistency.
  - core-03's Dialog Object section said "it is possible to have a Dialog Object with no parameters in
    it".
  - Its schema required `type` and `start`.
  - [section 7.1 of the vCon design page, "Section numbers"](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/docs/design/vcon.md#71-section-numbers),
    records where that text went.
- From 0.5.128 sipnab emitted such an object with no `type`.
  - Its vendored schema removed `type` from `required` as a documented deviation.

[Section 4.3 of core-04](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-4.3) replaced that sentence.

- It covers a dialog known to have occurred, with little or nothing captured from it.
- The object for it is a placeholder "which contains only the type parameter".
  - Its type is `recording` if the call reached setup.
  - Its type is `incomplete` if it did not.
- `start` became a SHOULD ([section 4.3.2](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-4.3.2)).

So sipnab dropped the deviation.

- Both vendored schema files are the publisher's core-04 file, byte for byte.
- Every Dialog Object sipnab writes names its type.

**The `type` follows what sipnab observed.**

- `incomplete`, from
  [section 4.3.1.5 of core-04](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-4.3.1.5), names a call that "failed to
  be setup".
- That is a claim about the CONVERSATION.
- sipnab emitted it for every signaling-only export until 0.5.128.
- So a successful call shipped a container reporting a setup failure.
- Read months later beside a switch's CDR showing a
  connected ninety-second call, the container is the thing that looks wrong.

sipnab now keeps `incomplete` for a dialog whose final response it OBSERVED to
be a failure.

- Every other signaling-only object is the `recording` placeholder.
- `dialog_object()` decides the type and the disposition in one expression.
- The reason: [section 4.3.11 of core-04](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-4.3.11) couples
  them.
  - An incomplete object MUST name a disposition.
  - A disposition is only nameable when sipnab saw a failure.
- The media path fills the placeholder in place when audio actually arrives.
  - It clears `disposition` with it.

A `recording` placeholder carries no `body` and no `url`.

- A conserver transcription link that selects `type == "recording"` and reads
  `dialog["url"]` with a bracket raises on it.
- Under core-03 the type-free object raised in the same links at `dialog["type"]`.
- The converse costs as much.
  - Every `type == "recording"` selector skips audio left on an `incomplete` object.
  - So the WAV would sit in the container unreachable.

`audio_never_rides_on_an_object_typed_incomplete` and
`a_recording_without_content_is_a_bare_placeholder` pin both directions.

- The second lives in the SIGNALING-ONLY test file on purpose.
- Over a media fixture every object has a body.
- So the assertion passes vacuously and the mutation survives.

**The repository carries the schema, so the gate runs offline.**

- [`tests/schemas/vcon.schema.json`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/tests/schemas/vcon.schema.json) is the
  working group's core-04 schema, vendored unchanged.
- [`tests/schemas/publisher/vcon_json_schema.json`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/tests/schemas/publisher/vcon_json_schema.json)
  holds the same bytes.
- `the_vendored_vcon_schema_is_the_publishers_core_04_file`
  pins both to the publisher's commit and SHA-256.
- So a re-vendor is a recorded change rather than an edit.

`a_container_validates_against_the_working_group_schema` in
[`tests/vcon_ingest_contract_test.rs`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/tests/vcon_ingest_contract_test.rs)
validates a real export against it.

- That one test found six violations.
- The hand-written assertions around it had all missed them.
- Those assertions encoded what we believed the format required.
- Add a field and this gate, not a reviewer, tells you whether the format agrees.

**Media enriches the signaling object rather than appending a second one.**

- A dialog is one conversation.
- A container that carries a `recording` object beside a separate signaling object
  describes it as two.
- When audio decodes, `export_dialog_at()` fills the existing object's fields in place:
  `start`, `duration`, `parties`, `mediatype`, `encoding`, `content_hash` and `body`.
- The one exception is a wrapped ring buffer.
  - There the retained audio genuinely is a subset of a longer call.
  - The object becomes a `recording-set` and the audio hangs beneath it.
  - That is what that type is for.

## Adding a field without breaking the divergence gate

The gate compares whole JSON objects. So the rule is short: **add the field to
`CaptureCompleteness`, and to nothing else.**

- Add the field to the struct.
  - Both surfaces serialize the same value, so both gain it at once.
  - The equality assertion still holds.
- Populate it in `completeness_of()`, from `ExportContext` and from nothing
  else.
  - Reading a process global here is what stops an export from reproducing.
- If the field describes a loss, add a clause to
  [`completeness_note()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/output/vcon.rs).
  - Then the prose surface says what the structured surface counts.
  - Write it as a measurement of the run, never as a conclusion about the call.
  - "the capture missed the answer" is a fact about the tap.
  - "the call went unanswered" is a fact about the traffic.
  - This module exists because vCon cannot tell them apart.
- Extend `the_completeness_carrier_discriminates_a_lossy_run_from_a_clean_one`
  with a run that moves the new field.
  - Without that, the clause is unproven.

What breaks the gate is building a value inside `report()` or inside
`completeness_attachment()`.

- Both take a `&CaptureCompleteness` and serialize it.
- Keep it that way.

Two adjacent rules an edit trips over:

- **Never put a caveat in `subject`.**
  - The core draft defines it as the topic of the conversation.
  - So a disclaimer there arrives styled as a fact about the call.
  - `the_container_declares_its_version_and_signs_nothing` asserts `subject`
    stays absent.
  - The same holds for `signatures`, `payload`, `protected`, `jwe`,
    `jws` and `consent`.
- **Never widen `failure_disposition()` below 400.**
  - A 3xx redirect did not fail.
  - A container claiming it did sends an operator after a fault that is not there.
  - The redirect case sits inside the mapping test on purpose.
  - So widening the range fails there rather than shipping.

## The uuid: deterministic by construction

[`dialog_uuid()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/output/vcon.rs) writes a UUIDv8 laid out like a
UUIDv7:

- a 48-bit millisecond timestamp;
- a 12-bit `rand_a`;
- a 62-bit `rand_b`.

Three choices make it a function of the observation rather than of the
run:

| Field | Source | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 48-bit timestamp | the **dialog's** `created_at` | the export clock here would mint a new identifier on every re-export |
| `rand_a`, 12 bits | SHA-256 of `Call-ID`, a `0x1e` separator, then `capture_id` | ties the value to the dialog and the capture it came from |
| `rand_b`, 62 bits | the high 62 bits of SHA-256 over the node name, a `0x1e` separator, the `Call-ID`, another separator, then `capture_id` | host-derived, as the draft asks, and dialog-derived as well — see the collision window below |

The separator byte matters. A bare concatenation collides `("ab", "c")` with
`("a", "bc")`.

The version and variant bits follow [RFC 9562](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9562.html):

- Version bits go in the high nibble of octet 6.
- The variant `10` goes in the two high bits of octet 8.
- `rand_b` shifts **down** by two rather than masking its top bits off.
- So the variant bits overwrite nothing the draft asked for.

`created_at` still carries the export time, where the draft puts it.

- Two exports of one dialog days apart therefore share a uuid.
- They differ in `created_at`.
- `the_uuid_separates_dialogs_captures_and_clocks` asserts exactly that pair.

**The collision window, and how it closed.**

- Until 0.5.125 this keyed `rand_b` on the node ALONE.
  - It spent 62 of the 74 available bits on a value identical for every dialog on the box.
- Two dialogs opening in the same millisecond on one node had 12 bits between them.
  - So roughly one pair in 4096 collided.
- [section 4.1.2 of the core draft](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-4.1.2) makes the uuid globally unique.
  - The reason: a store KEYS on it.

A collision raises nothing.

- It overwrites the record already there.
- That loses one capture with no error anywhere.

An earlier version of this page called that "inherent in the layout the draft
asks for". It is not.

- The draft asks for a host-derived value in `rand_b`.
- It never asks for a value derived from the host and NOTHING ELSE.
- Folding the dialog and the capture into the same digest keeps every property the layout wanted.
- It takes the discriminating bits from 12 to 74.

Determinism is the property that had to survive, and it did.

- The digest is over stable inputs.
- So re-exporting one dialog from one capture still yields one identifier.
- `two_dialogs_in_one_millisecond_on_one_node_get_different_uuids`
  holds a real colliding pair found by brute force.
- It asserts the precondition that they still share the old 12-bit bucket.
- So it fails loudly rather than passing vacuously if the seed ever changes.

One more substitution to know about: the draft fills `rand_b` with SHA-1 of a
host name alone, and the default does not.

- UUIDv8 constrains only the version and variant bits.
  - This function writes both.
- What changes is which bits land in `rand_b`.

**`[vcon] uuid_domain` follows the draft's form.**

- `UuidDomain` holds the name and the high 62 bits of SHA-1 over it, from
  the `sha1` crate the `vcon` feature already carries for RSA-OAEP.
- `bootstrap::declare_process_globals` declares it once, so every door mints
  the same uuid for one dialog.
- `rand_b` is the domain's 62 bits. `rand_a` keeps the default's seed.
- That leaves 12 bits per millisecond per domain, so `UuidSlots` records the
  `rand_a` values given out per millisecond and steps a colliding seed to the
  next free value.
  - It is per process and capped at `UUID_SLOT_CAP` identities, oldest
    milliseconds dropped first.
- `revision_uuid` takes the same path for a `new-uuid` chain.
- Tests: `the_default_uuid_is_byte_identical_to_before` pins the default from
  before the key existed. `a_domain_uuid_follows_the_section_4_1_2_layout`
  recomputes each field. `two_dialogs_in_one_millisecond_get_different_domain_uuids`
  holds a seed collision found by search. [`tests/vcon_uuid_domain_test.rs`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/tests/vcon_uuid_domain_test.rs)
  covers the shipped binary.
- See [The uuid under a domain](@/docs/vcon.md#the-uuid-under-a-domain).

## The credential strip, and what it does today

[`strip_credentials()`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/output/vcon.rs) walks a JSON value at every
depth. It drops any key matching `CREDENTIAL_HEADERS`:

- `Authorization`;
- `Proxy-Authorization`;
- `WWW-Authenticate`;
- `Proxy-Authenticate`.

It compares case-insensitively.

- SIP header names are case-insensitive on the wire.
- A filter keyed on exact case is one an ordinary peer walks through.

`Proxy-Authenticate` is on the list although the SIP-signaling extension names
only three.

- It is the proxy-side twin of `WWW-Authenticate`.
- It carries the same realm and nonce.
- Leaving it off would hold the rule for one hop and not the other.

**It is load-bearing as of 0.5.125.** It was not before.

- The honest history matters more than the current state.
- The reason: the shape of the mistake recurs.

The filter used to guard a projection that could not carry a credential.

- `message_to_json_value()` had no raw header map.
- So no message reached it with a banned key.
- `no_credential_survives_an_export` planted a real `Authorization`
  and a real `Proxy-Authorization` in its fixture and passed.
  - It passed not because the filter worked, but because the field did not exist.
- A regression gate for something that could not regress reads exactly like a working control.
  - That holds in a coverage report and to a reviewer.

The old text here predicted its own resolution: "giving that projection a
`headers` field is an ordinary, sensible change to a debugging surface, and it
would start putting digest credentials into a container that leaves this
machine."

- That is what 0.5.125 did.
- The two halves landed in ONE change, deliberately.

The reasons:

- The `sip-signaling` extension names `headers` in its message structure.
- A SIP trace without them is a summary of a trace.
- So the field was going to arrive.
- A field that publishes credentials must never land in a
  release ahead of the filter that removes them.

The filter is now mutation-proven end to end.

- Empty `CREDENTIAL_HEADERS` and `no_credential_survives_an_export` fails.
- That is the thing it always claimed to check.

Three tests keep the distinction visible:

- `the_trace_carries_the_headers_the_filter_exists_to_clean` is the half that
  keeps the other two honest.
  - Drop `headers` from the trace and the filter has nothing to remove again.
  - So it fails rather than letting the pair go quietly back to proving nothing.
- `the_credential_filter_removes_banned_headers_at_every_depth` runs against a
  hand-built value.
  - So it covers nesting depths an ordinary export never produces.
  - It is mutation-proven: deleting the `retain` fails it.
  - Its anti-vacuity assertions fail a filter that emptied the object instead.
- `no_credential_survives_an_export` is the end-to-end half.
  - It passes on the strength of the projection rather than of the filter.
  - It is what refuses the digest response the day that changes.

## Reading a container back

The reader is a separate module,
[`capture/vcon_input.rs`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/capture/vcon_input.rs). It is an
input source rather than part of the exporter.

- It rebuilds each message of a `sip-message-trace` attachment, or each
  `message/sip` attachment, as wire text.
- It hands it to the packet path as a pre-parsed packet.
  - So nothing downstream has a vCon branch.
- What it cannot rebuild it records in a `VconProvenance`.
  - The capture analysis turns that into the `rebuilt_from_vcon` finding.
- The inline analysis behind the MCP `analyze_vcon` tool and `POST /v1/vcon/analyze`
  is [`output/vcon_analysis.rs`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/src/output/vcon_analysis.rs).
  - It is one function for both surfaces.

A schema finding never stops a read. It rides in the provenance.

- The reader refuses only two things:
  - a container whose SIP it cannot rebuild;
  - a JSON object with none of the members a vCon has.
- A change to the trace the exporter writes is a change to what the reader can rebuild.
- So [`tests/vcon_input_test.rs`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/tests/vcon_input_test.rs) exports a capture
  with the built binary and reads it back.
  - It compares every stored field.

## What the tests cover

Unit tests live in the module and reach its private helpers.
[`tests/vcon_export_test.rs`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/tests/vcon_export_test.rs) is the other half.
It proves two things the unit tests structurally cannot:

- that the whole export is reachable through the crate's **public** surface;
- that a dialog off a real parsed capture carries what the hand-built fixtures carry.

A projection can agree with a synthetic dialog and disagree with the parser.

Both halves gate on the feature. So a build without `vcon` compiles neither.

The schema validator in `vcon_schema.rs` also runs over containers sipnab
did not build: the public vCon datasets.

- A committed subset runs on every build.
- All 17,443 containers run on request.
- [Testing](@/docs/internals/testing.md#the-public-vcon-datasets) says how to fetch them and what they get.

## Decisions and history behind the operator page

The operator page, [Export one observed call as a vCon](@/docs/vcon.md), says what
each setting does. The reasons, the release history and the measurements
behind it live here.

### Why the export is behind a feature

- `vcon` is a non-default Cargo feature, as every capture-side publication
  feature is. A container that leaves the machine is a publication surface,
  and a capture tool grows one only when an operator asks for it.
- The TUI has no export key binding. The binding would do nothing in a build
  without the feature, so the TUI help names the REST route and the feature
  flag instead.
- sipnab refuses `--vcon-out` without `--export-vcon` because a path with nothing
  to write to it is a mistake, and naming it beats ignoring it.
- sipnab refuses a `--vcon-out` that names the capture it reads because an export that
  overwrites its own evidence destroys the input.

### Why `grouping = "leg"` is the default

- A PBX that copies no identifier between legs leaves one tie: the timing
  guess from shared addresses and close start times.
- Grouping on a wrong guess puts two unrelated calls in one container.
- A per-call container states every tie sipnab built it on, so a reader can see
  when that happened; the per-leg default never merges on a guess.

### Ceilings the operator page states as numbers

Each of these is a bound an operator can meet. The operator page gives the
number, and this table names the constant.

| Constant | What it bounds |
|---|---|
| `MAX_PACKET` (1275) | The largest Opus packet the Ogg Opus writer emits, in bytes: the largest [RFC 6716 section 3.4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6716.html#section-3.4) allows |
| `MAX_PACKETS_PER_PASS` (10) | RTP packets a `live_rtp` leg sends per 20 ms pass when audio waits in the queue: ten times real time |
| `MAX_SIGNED_LAYERS` (16) | Nested JWS layers a reader walks before it refuses a container |
| `MAX_ISSUER_LEN` (8192) | Characters in the SCITT `scitt_issuer` URI |
| `MAX_POLLS` (16) | Polls of a SCITT `202` receipt location |
| `MAX_RECEIPT` (65536) | Bytes of a SCITT receipt sipnab keeps |
| `MAX_FINDING_TAGS` (5) | `finding:` tags in a rule's `tags` attachment |
| `MAX_KEY_PRESSES` (256) | Telephone events kept per RTP stream for `party_history` |
| `MAX_CONTAINER_BYTES` (67,108,864) | The size of one container a reader accepts, 64 MiB |

### The encrypted form before 0.5.219

sipnab 0.5.217 and 0.5.218 wrote `alg` and `enc` in a JWE `protected` member,
and `x5c` in the signature's protected header. Core-04 section 5.2 places
`x5c` in the unprotected `header`, and later releases write it there, with no
JWE `protected` member. The readers and the fetcher still open the older
layout.

### Conformance against the draft's own example

The JOSE tests check sipnab against the encrypted example of
draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04 Appendix A.7: sipnab decrypts that example and
verifies its signature, and signs the same bytes with the same key to the
same signature.

### Why the spool stages in the destination directory

`rename` is atomic only within one filesystem. Across a mount boundary it
fails or degrades into a copy, and a copy puts a partial file back in view.
So sipnab stages a container as `.<container>.partial` in the destination
directory, flushes it, and renames it into place. For the same reason the
forwarder's delivered and failed directories must be on the spool's
filesystem.

### Why `--vcon-digest` is not a signature

The digest is a SHA-256 of the bytes sipnab wrote, kept outside the container.
A store adds fields on ingest, so a signature over sipnab's bytes would fail
against the object the store holds and tell an operator nothing. The opt-in
JWS of a signing rule is a separate mechanism, over the container the rule
writes.

### Store behavior the forwarder and fetcher kinds encode

The per-kind values come from these observations and sources.

- vcon.store, 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-11: the measurements in
  [vCon delivery pages: measurements and history](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/docs/design/vcon-store-and-harness-notes.md#the-measurements).
  It answered `500` to a uuid it already held on 2026-10-09 and `409` by
  2026-10-11. Its read path and
  `_meta` envelope come from its OpenAPI document and a `GET` that returned
  the container's members and `_meta`.
- A self-hosted conserver, 2026-10-07, sent a synthetic container from the
  test fixtures:
  - `204` for a new container; `GET /vcon/{uuid}` then returned it with an
    `amended` member added.
  - `204` for the same uuid sent again; the read-back showed the second copy.
  - `422` for a body that is not JSON, and for one without `uuid`.
  - `403` with no key or a wrong one.
- The conserver kind's read path is from `api/api.py` of `vcon-dev/vcon-server`;
  the vcon-mcp kind's from `src/api/routes/vcons.ts`, `src/api/rest-router.ts`
  and `src/api/auth.ts` of `vcon-dev/vcon-mcp`.
- The forwarder's default `Content-Type` stays `application/json` because on
  2026-10-14 a self-hosted conserver answered `422` to a container sent as
  `application/vcon`, and `204` to the same container as `application/json`
  or `application/vcon+json`.
- On 2026-10-14 the same conserver answered `500` to a gzip format body sent
  as `application/vcon+gzip`, and `400` (`There was an error parsing the
  body`) to the same body as `application/json` with `Content-Encoding: gzip`.
- On 2026-10-13 that conserver answered `204` to an encrypted container. It
  ran a vcon-server branch that adds encrypted vCon ingest; how an unmodified
  vcon-server answers a signed or encrypted container was not measured.
- No kind sets a `--vcon-forward-replace-url`. The operator page recorded that
  nobody had measured a `PUT` to vcon.store.
- A self-hosted conserver once answered `204` for a container it then failed
  to write, with nothing in the answer saying so. That is why the forwarder
  logs `delivered`, never `stored`.
- The 5 MiB default of `--vcon-max-inline-media` comes from the store
  measurement recorded in [the vCon design decision](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/docs/design/vcon.md): a
  store answered `204` for a container of roughly 12 MB, wrote it to its
  database, had its own file spool refuse the payload, and neither side
  reported the partial write.

### Format changes the operator page used to narrate

- The message trace's `version` member became the string `"1.0"`, the trace
  format version draft-howe-vcon-sip-signaling-00 defines. Before that it was
  the number `1`. `schema_version` stays the number `1`.
- Before draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04 support, a Dialog Object with no content
  carried no `type`, as core-03 allowed. Core-04 requires `type`, so such an
  object is now `"type": "recording"` with no `body` or `url`.
- `Party::name` carries the display name from `From` or `To`, beside
  `sip_display_name`. An earlier version of the operator page said the type
  had no `name` field, which was wrong, and would have led a reader to redact
  only `sip_display_name`.
